title: A Lab-On-A-Chip Platform for Stimulating Osteocyte Mechanotransduction and Analyzing Functional Outcomes of Bone Remodeling
protocol: Cover the top surface of the mask with plastic sheeting.
Secure the chip mask to an equally sized acrylic sheet using spray adhesive.
Clamp the pieces together overnight to allow the adhesive to fully cure.
Remove the plastic sheeting from the top of the mask after the adhesive is dry.
Attach the bottom of the acrylic sheet to a 3D printed leveling box using double-sided tape.
Press firmly to ensure a tight bond between the acrylic sheet and the leveling box.
Seal any small openings near the detachable wall of the leveling box with a waterproof sealant.
Allow the sealant to cure for 24 hours.
Clean the surface of the mask with 70% ethanol.
Place the leveling box with the desired chip mask in the oven.
Use a digital protractor to ensure the top of the mask is level.
Adjust the leveling screws if necessary.
Combine 63 g of PDMS prepolymer and 6.3 g of curing agent in a plastic cup.
Mix thoroughly with a disposable cell spatula.
Degas the mixture in a vacuum desiccator for 30 min.
Slowly pour the mixture into the prepared leveling box.
Let the PDMS sit for 30 min.
Bake at 45 °C for 18 h.
Loosen the edges of the PDMS with a tapered laboratory spatula.
Remove the polymer sheet from the leveling box.
Cut individual lids to size (70 mm x 34 mm) using a scalpel and a 3D printed template.
Punch access holes through each lid with a biopsy punch (1 mm diameter).
Surface clean the lids with packaging tape.
If not used immediately, wrap each lid in packaging tape and store at room temperature.
Combine PDMS prepolymer and curing agent in a plastic cup.
Mix vigorously and degas for 30 min.
Pour mixture over appropriate pre-leveled mask.
Let the PDMS sit for 30 min.
Bake at 45 °C for 18 h.
Loosen the edges of the PDMS with a tapered laboratory spatula.
Carefully peel the polymer away from the mask.
Use a scalpel and 3D printed template to cut out individual chips.
Add 12.7 g of PDMS prepolymer and 1.3 g of curing agent (10:1 ratio) to a plastic cup.
Mix vigorously and degas for 30 min.
Slowly pour polymer into prepared leveling box and thoroughly scrape plastic cup to remove as much PDMS as possible.
Spread PDMS over entire surface using cell spatula.
Let the PDMS sit for 30 min and then bake at 45 °C for 18 h.
Loosen the edges of the PDMS with a tapered spatula and carefully remove the PDMS sheet from the leveling box.
Cut individual membranes that match the dimensions of layer 2.
Measure the membrane thickness at the center of the membrane using calipers.
Discard any membranes that are outside of the desired thickness (0.5 mm ± 0.1 mm).
Clean membranes with packaging tape and place on a piece of paraffin film.
Place masking tape on the back side of a tissue culture treated polystyrene coverslip.
Cut circular discs from the coverslip using a sharpened cork-borer (5.4 mm diameter).
Submerge the discs in 70% EtOH and leave overnight.
Gently scrub the top surface of the disc with a cotton tipped applicator soaked in 70% EtOH.
Ensure that the outer edge of the disc is thoroughly cleaned.
Remove the masking tape backing from the disc using two pairs of forceps.
Place the disc treated side down into the well and clean the back side with a cotton tipped applicator.
Dip the wooden end of a cotton tipped applicator into a degassed mixture of uncured PDMS and place a small amount on the bottom of the desired well.
Hold the polystyrene disc, treated side up, into the well using two pairs of forceps and gently press down with a cotton swab to ensure no uncured PDMS contacts the treated side.
If PDMS contacts the treated surface, remove the disc from the well and repeat steps involving cleaning and attaching the disc.
Let the chip sit on a level surface for 30 min.
Bake the chip at 65 °C for 4 h.
Use forceps to place a bone wafer on the bottom of a 100 mm dish.
Gently etch an 'X' on the back of the wafer with a scalpel.
Add a small amount of uncured PDMS to the bottom of the desired well using the wooden end of a cotton tipped applicator.
Place the bone wafer, marked side down, into the well.
Press the wafer down gently with a cotton tipped applicator.
Let the chip sit on a level surface for 30 min.
Bake the chip at 65 °C for 4 h.
Activate the surfaces of layer 1 and layer 2 with a plasma cleaner for 30 s using medium radio frequency power.
Align the access holes in layer 1 with the microchannels in layer 2.
Firmly press the two layers together.
For the deep-well design, repeat step 4.1 with layer 2 and layer 3.
Attach the paraffin film of layer 3 to a flat surface using double-sided tape during plasma treatment.
Trim off excess material from the PDMS membrane using a scalpel.
Carefully peel away the sheet of paraffin film from the bottom of the chip.
Bake the chip at 65 °C for 10 min.
Insert angled dispensing tips (18 Gauge, 0.5 in, 90°) into the access holes in the lid.
Secure the dispensing tips to the lid with a two part epoxy.
Use a micropipette tip to apply the epoxy around each dispensing tip.
Surface clean the chip with 70% EtOH and place it in a biosafety cabinet.
Connect a 5 mL syringe to the dispensing tips with sterile silicone tubing (1/32'' ID, ~10 cm in length).
Fill the entire chip with 70% EtOH for at least 30 seconds.
For the shallow-well design, administer all liquids with a syringe pump set to a flow rate of 4 mL/h.
For the deep-well design, slowly dispense the syringe by hand to administer all liquids.
Remove the EtOH from the chip and sterilize the chip with UV light overnight.
Wash the chip three times with dH2O.
Fill the chip with dH2O, remove tubing from the dispensing tips.
Incubate the filled chip for at least 48 hours at 37 °C.
Use a 5 mL syringe to remove dH2O from the deep-well chip following step 4.9.
Coat the bottom of the well with 200 μL of 0.15 mg/mL type I collagen in 0.02 M acetic acid for 1 h.
Rinse the chip three times with Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline with calcium and magnesium (DPBS++).
Place chip into the chip holder.
Seed the chip with MLO-Y4 osteocytes at a density of 2 x 10^4 cells/mL in minimum essential alpha medium supplemented with 5% calf serum, 5% fetal bovine serum, and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
Remove tubing from dispensing tips.
Place the chip into a deep-well culture dish (150 mm x 25 mm).
Incubate cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 72 h.
Attach sterile tubing to dispensing tips.
Use a 5 mL syringe to remove spent culture medium from the chip.
Slowly dispense fresh culture medium into the chip to refill it.
Place the chip holder into the rectangular inset on top of the loading device base.
Feed the tubing through slots located on the loading device lid.
Secure the lid to the base with four pan head screws and hex nuts, ensuring the lid remains level by securing two diagonally positioned screws first before the others.
Turn the dial clockwise until the desired platen displacement is reached.
Place the loading device into an empty P1000 micropipette tip box.
Incubate the cells with the applied load for 15 min.
Remove the load from the cells by turning the dial counterclockwise until the platen returns to the original starting position.
Remove the lid from the device and place the chip holder into the deep-well culture plate.
Incubate the cells for a 90-min post-load recovery period.
Feed cells every 72 h for long-term studies.
Use a 5 mL syringe to remove the conditioned medium from the chip.
Remove the chip from the chip holder.
Use a tapered spatula to break the bond between the PDMS lid and well layer.
